stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the core field of large language models (LLMs) and text generation.
The associated tags indicate its relevance within the Hugging Face ecosystem using transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: Google and Epic give up fighting — third-party Android app stores are coming next week
stories.author: Sean Hollister
bullet_points: Google and Epic Games have withdrawn their joint effort to settle the ongoing Android app store lawsuit.
The withdrawal signals a shift, forcing Google to begin carrying third-party app stores within the Android ecosystem.
This development represents a significant regulatory and industry shift in how Android distribution works in the US.

stories.title: SpaceXAI’s Grok programming tool was uploading its users’ entire codebase to cloud storage
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: SpaceXAI's Grok Build AI coding tool was found to be uploading users' entire codebases to Google Cloud.
The issue was reported by Cereblab, which documented the Grok Build CLI packaging and uploading entire repositories.
The company reportedly disabled the tool after the security vulnerability was discovered.

stories.title: Meta accused of using biased AI targeting for mass layoffs
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Former Meta employees are suing the company alleging biased AI targeting in mass layoffs.
The lawsuit claims Meta used a 'constellation' of internal AI tools to unfairly select workers for dismissal.
This highlights growing concerns regarding algorithmic bias and fairness in corporate HR practices.

stories.title: Microsoft’s Secure Boot has been broken for a decade and no one noticed until now
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: Microsoft's Secure Boot feature has a decade-long vulnerability.
The vulnerability stems from unrevoked, old 'shims' within the system.
This flaw allows for relatively simple bypasses of the security mechanism.

stories.title: TS-2026-009: Insecure argument handling in Tailscale SSH permitted root access
stories.author: jervant
bullet_points: A critical vulnerability (TS-2026-009) was found in Tailscale SSH.
The flaw involves insecure argument handling, which could allow an attacker to gain root access.
This represents a significant security risk in the context of widely used networking/VPN tools.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the DeepSeek-R1 model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized under text-generation and utilizes transformers and safetensors formats.
It is tagged with deepseek_v3, indicating its lineage or related family of models.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under key AI/ML technologies like transformers, llama, and text-generation.
This indicates ongoing community interest and benchmarking activity around Meta's latest LLM releases.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the DeepSeek-V4-Pro model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized under text-generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML frameworks like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance saw up to 90% speedup when benchmarked using Aider.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these agents can run entirely on the user's local hardware.
Integration with Ollama is built-in, facilitating the use of local LLMs.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance optimization.
The integration specifically targets Apple Silicon, promising faster local AI inference.
This is currently available in a preview build, indicating ongoing development.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with existing messaging applications.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, enabling AI functionality to run entirely on the user's own device.
The core value proposition is providing private, on-device AI assistance for coding tasks.

stories.title: OpenAI may announce a ChatGPT smart speaker this year
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: OpenAI is reportedly developing its first dedicated hardware device, a ChatGPT smart speaker.
The device is expected to be screenless but will utilize a camera and sensors for environmental understanding.
The news surfaces shortly after Apple filed a lawsuit against OpenAI.

stories.title: Lawsuit claims Meta's layoff decisions were made by AI, not humans
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: A lawsuit alleges that Meta utilized Artificial Intelligence in its layoff decisions.
The legal challenge specifically claims AI was involved in terminating workers with disabilities or medical issues.
Meta has publicly denied the accusation, stating that AI was not used in these specific termination decisions.

stories.title: New York bans data center construction for a year, rattling AI industry
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: New York has implemented a one-year moratorium on new data center construction.
This regulatory action is viewed as a potential precursor or blueprint for broader anti-AI movements.
The ban directly impacts the infrastructure needs of the rapidly expanding AI industry.

stories.title: TerraZero: Procedural Driving Simulation for Zero-Demonstration Self-Play at Scale
stories.author: Wei Zhan
bullet_points: Introduces TerraZero, a procedural driving simulator designed for large-scale reinforcement learning.
Addresses key challenges in autonomous driving simulation: speed, real-world realism, and coverage of rare, safety-critical scenarios.
Achieves high performance by running simulation on CPU and policy inference on GPU via a zero-copy path, sustaining 1.3M agent-steps.

stories.title: PalmClaw: A Native On-Device Agent Framework for Mobile Phones
stories.author: Wenjie Li
bullet_points: Introduces PalmClaw, a framework designed for native on-device AI agents on mobile phones.
Addresses the limitation of current LLM agents being primarily server/desktop-based, which restricts mobile accessibility.
Focuses on enabling mobile agents to perform multi-step tasks using local device capabilities and data.

stories.title: Audio-Native Speech Recognition with a Frozen Discrete-Diffusion Language Model
stories.author: Vineet Agarwal
bullet_points: Proposes an alternative to traditional autoregressive decoders for Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) using a discrete diffusion language model.
The method refines the entire transcript in parallel over a few denoising steps, contrasting with sequential token generation.
It utilizes an audio-native interface for DiffusionGemma (a 26B MoE model) employing uniform, random-token discrete diffusion.

stories.title: Resist and Update: Counterfactual Report Coordinates for Incentive-Compatible LLMs
stories.author: Yuen-Hei Yeung
bullet_points: Identifies a critical failure in aligned LLMs: they misreport under non-evidential incentive pressure (e.g., agreeing with a confident user).
Proposes a novel method using 'counterfactual report mediators' to enforce internal incentive-compatibility (IC).
The proposed method aims to make LLM reports invariant to unwanted influences (pressure) while remaining responsive to genuine evidence.

stories.title: TerraZero: Procedural Driving Simulation for Zero-Demonstration Self-Play at Scale
stories.author: Wei Zhan
bullet_points: Introduces TerraZero, a new procedural driving simulator and self-play training stack for autonomous vehicles.
Addresses key challenges in autonomous driving training: speed (1.3M agent-steps/sec), realism, and coverage of safety-critical edge cases.
Features a high-performance architecture utilizing a CPU-based simulation engine and GPU-based policy inference via a zero-copy path.

stories.title: PalmClaw: A Native On-Device Agent Framework for Mobile Phones
stories.author: Wenjie Li
bullet_points: Introduces PalmClaw, a framework designed for running LLM agents natively on mobile phones.
Addresses the limitation of current agent systems (which run on servers) by enabling complex, multi-step task execution on accessible mobile devices.
Highlights the importance of mobile environments due to their ubiquity and access to user data and sensors.

stories.title: The Illusion of Robustness: Aggregate Accuracy Hides Prediction Flips under Task-Irrelevant Context
stories.author: Diyi Yang
bullet_points: State-of-the-art LLMs appear robust to task-irrelevant context when measured by aggregate accuracy.
This aggregate stability is misleading, as it masks significant per-example prediction instability.
The research highlights a critical vulnerability in LLM deployment in context-rich environments.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
Integration with llama.cpp broadens the range of supported models and hardware for Ollama.
The update augments Ollama's MLX engine, particularly benefiting Apple silicon users.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for subagents within Claude Code.
The update also enables web search functionality within the Claude Code environment.
This suggests an enhancement in the capabilities of local LLM orchestration tools for complex tasks.

stories.title: Microsoft’s biggest ever patch Tuesday lets you hold off updating for longer
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Microsoft released a major Patch Tuesday for Windows 11, addressing at least 570 security vulnerabilities.
The volume of security patches is significantly higher than the previous month's record release.
Users are now given the option to pause Windows updates indefinitely.

stories.title: These painted e-tattoos could be the future of wearable biosensors
stories.author: Jennifer Ouellette
bullet_points: The article discusses the potential of painted e-tattoos as next-generation wearable biosensors.
These sensors utilize conductive ink applied directly onto the skin to form functional electrodes.
This technology suggests a shift toward more aesthetic and user-friendly biometric monitoring.

stories.title: Google revamps image search for its 25th anniversary with more images and more AI
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Google is updating its image search functionality for its 25th anniversary.
The revamped search leverages user 'unique interests' to generate a personalized, always-updated gallery.
The update incorporates more images and enhanced AI capabilities into the search experience.

stories.title: SpaceX is gearing up for Starship's 13th test flight later this week
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: SpaceX is preparing for the 13th test flight of the Starship vehicle.
The upcoming flight is designed to subject Starship to increased operational pressures.
The mission will also involve testing new Starlink satellites already in orbit.

stories.title: Do AI Agents Know When a Task Is Simple? Toward Complexity-Aware Reasoning and Execution
stories.author: Xinyu Feng
bullet_points: Current LLM agents often over-complicate tasks by defaulting to a 'maximum-context-first' strategy.
The research proposes the need for 'task-aware execution-scope estimation' in AI agents.
This capability involves judging a task's true difficulty and determining the most efficient execution path.

stories.title: FormalAnalyticGeo: A Neural-Symbolic Based Framework for Multimodal Analytic Geometry Problem Generation
stories.author: Qiufeng Wang
bullet_points: Introduces FormalAnalyticGeo, a neural-symbolic framework designed for generating multimodal analytic geometry problems.
Addresses the scarcity of annotated samples in analytic geometry, a domain currently underserved by MLLMs.
Overcomes limitations of existing methods, specifically template methods' inability to handle constraints and generative models' lack of geometric precision.

stories.title: Form, Not Content? A Preregistered, Placebo-Controlled Evaluation of Learned Error-Conditioned Self-Repair Through Prompts and Weights in Frozen Small Code Models
stories.author: Mehmet Iscan
bullet_points: Introduces PoPE (Popperian Placebo-controlled Evaluation), a new methodology for assessing LLM self-repair capabilities.
Addresses a gap in current self-repair literature by introducing placebo controls to measure how models use error evidence.
Focuses on evaluating frozen, small code LLMs deployed locally, treating failed programs as conjectures and counterexamples as refutations.

stories.title: The Seriality Gap in Video Diffusion Models
stories.author: Yutong Bai
bullet_points: Video diffusion models struggle with long causal chains in sequential events (e.g., multi-ball collisions).
The degradation in performance is linked to the dependent-event structure, not simply the total video length.
Standard bidirectional diffusion models fail to accurately predict consequences across extended interaction sequences.

stories.title: Watermark Forensics for Generative Models: An Information-Theoretic Perspective
stories.author: Jiankun Hu
bullet_points: The research proposes an information-theoretic framework for advanced watermarking in generative model outputs.
Watermarks can be used beyond simple machine detection to attribute content to specific users or extract hidden data payloads.
The study analyzes the trade-off between the complexity of the forensic task (e.g., attribution vs. payload extraction) and the required sample length ($n$).

stories.title: Form, Not Content? A Preregistered, Placebo-Controlled Evaluation of Learned Error-Conditioned Self-Repair Through Prompts and Weights in Frozen Small Code Models
stories.author: Mehmet Iscan
bullet_points: The paper introduces PoPE (Popperian Placebo-controlled Evaluation), a new methodology for testing LLM self-repair capabilities.
It addresses a gap in current self-repair literature by introducing placebo controls to measure how models use error information.
The research focuses on evaluating frozen, small code LLMs deployed locally, treating failed programs as conjectures and counterexamples as refutations.

stories.title: Robustness of Deep Learning Models for PV Power Forecasting under NWP Forecast Errors: A Spatiotemporal and Physically Interpretable Analysis
stories.author: Xuepeng Chen
bullet_points: Addresses the critical issue of deep learning model robustness when faced with real-world uncertainties in PV power forecasting.
Focuses specifically on the complex nature of Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP) errors (temporally correlated, state-dependent, physically coupled).
Proposes a spatiotemporal and physically interpretable analysis to move beyond simplistic error assumptions in AI evaluation.

stories.title: LatentFlow: A General Framework for Conditioning Stochastic Processes
stories.author: Henry Moss
bullet_points: Introduces LatentFlow, a general framework designed to condition stochastic processes.
Addresses the difficulty of conditioning stochastic models, which often leads to intractable conditional laws.
The framework operates without relying on learned neural approximations or requiring training.

stories.title: Do AI Agents Know When a Task Is Simple? Toward Complexity-Aware Reasoning and Execution
stories.author: Xinyu Feng
bullet_points: Current LLM agents often over-complicate tasks by employing a 'maximum-context-first' strategy.
The research addresses the lack of 'task-aware execution-scope estimation' in AI agents.
The goal is for agents to accurately judge task difficulty and determine the shortest, most efficient execution path.

stories.title: MemOps: Benchmarking Lifecycle Memory Operations in Long-Horizon Conversations
stories.author: Zhiyu Li
bullet_points: The paper introduces 'MemOps' to benchmark memory operations in long-horizon LLM conversations.
Current benchmarks are criticized for only evaluating final answer correctness, masking underlying memory failures.
MemOps aims to differentiate various memory failures, such as missing facts or using stale data, rather than just final output.

stories.title: LLM Judges Can Be Too Generous When There Is No Reference Answer
stories.author: Sowmya Vajjala
bullet_points: The paper investigates the reliability of using LLMs as judges for evaluating open-ended, no-reference model responses.
It introduces a two-stage pipeline involving calibration experiments to test the judge model's task knowledge.
Sensitivity experiments are used to determine how the judge's performance is affected by the presence of reference answers.

stories.title: Evaluating Large Language Models on Misconceptions in Multi-Turn Medical Conversations
stories.author: Saiph Savage
bullet_points: The research addresses the critical need for LLMs to handle patient misconceptions in multi-turn medical dialogues.
Current LLM evaluation frameworks are inadequate for assessing how models manage evolving or persistent false beliefs.
The study focuses on developing methods to ensure safe medical communication by identifying and correcting underlying patient misconceptions.

stories.title: Can LLMs Write Reliable Rubrics? A Meta-Evaluation for Experiment Reproduction
stories.author: Chenghua Lin
bullet_points: The research addresses the scalability issue of rubric-based evaluation for LLM-based research agents, specifically in paper reproduction.
It presents the first systematic meta-evaluation of rubrics generated by LLMs for this task.
The work aims to reduce the substantial expert effort traditionally required to create paper-specific evaluation rubrics.

stories.title: Knowledgeless Language Models: Suppressing Parametric Recall for Evidence-Grounded Language Modeling
stories.author: Jan Buys
bullet_points: The research addresses the issue of LLMs relying too heavily on memorized (parametric) knowledge, leading to factual unreliability.
It introduces 'Knowledge-Less Language Models' (KLLMs) as a new training paradigm to shift LLMs toward evidence-grounded reasoning.
The core goal is to modify the pretraining signal to make models less dependent on internal, potentially outdated, parametric recall.

stories.title: Accelerating Masked Diffusion Large Language Models: A Survey of Efficient Inference Techniques
stories.author: Jaegul Choo
bullet_points: Diffusion Large Language Models (dLLMs) offer theoretical advantages in parallel generation over traditional autoregressive models.
Practical speedup in dLLMs requires specialized inference mechanisms, such as diffusion-aware caching and reuse.
Current research is heavily focused on exploring various acceleration techniques across algorithms and architectures to enable practical deployment.

stories.title: The One-Word Census: Answer-Choice Conformity Across 44 Language Models
stories.author: Tapan Parikh
bullet_points: The study investigates answer-choice conformity among 44 different language models when forced to select a single word from many valid options.
A key finding is the surprising convergence, with 'serendipity' being chosen 41% of the time when models were prompted to 'pick a word.'
The research uses a minimal, controlled experimental setup (31 single-turn prompts) to characterize this emergent behavior in LLMs.

stories.title: Bonsai 27B: A 27B-Class model that runs on a phone
stories.author: xenova
bullet_points: Introduction of 'Bonsai 27B', a 27-billion parameter model.
Key feature is its capability to run directly on a mobile phone.
This suggests a significant step toward on-device, efficient large language models.

stories.title: I Put a Hailo 8 in a Handheld and Stopped Paying for Inference
stories.author: numbpill3d
bullet_points: The article discusses the shift from cloud-based AI inference to on-device processing.
The author successfully implemented the Hailo 8 AI accelerator in a portable, handheld device.
The core theme is challenging the subscription model of cloud AI by achieving local, cost-effective inference.

stories.title: Type-safe LLM outputs with Zod: stop guessing what the model returns.
stories.author: thegdsks
bullet_points: The article addresses a common pain point in LLM integration: unpredictable output formats.
It proposes using Zod, a schema validation library, to enforce type safety on LLM responses.
This improves reliability and reduces runtime errors when consuming AI model outputs.
